title: Atoms & Tuples: Modeling Structured Telecom Events
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates tagged tuple construction, element extraction, and field swapping using pattern matching.

otpDocCards.description: Returns the number of elements in a tuple in O(1) time.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) BIF reading the tuple header arity word directly.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is comparing two atoms like (Status =:= active) faster than comparing two strings like ("active" =:= "active")?

options.label: Because strings are compiled to regular expressions in Erlang
options.explanation: Strings in Erlang are lists of integer codepoints, not regexes.

options.label: Because atoms are interned in a global table, reducing comparison to a single-cycle integer pointer check
options.explanation: Atoms exist once in the Atom Table. Comparing them is an O(1) pointer comparison; comparing strings requires traversing list nodes.

options.label: Because atoms are stored directly in CPU registers rather than on the heap
options.explanation: Atoms are represented as tagged pointer words referencing the Atom Table.
